description: DoS threat quantification on the HIP base-exchange (de-probabilised, after Basagiannis-Katsaros-Pombortsis-Alexiou COMPSAC 2008). The attacker counterfeits and replays R1 messages (the puzzle is unsigned), filling the Initiator's admission queue (capacity B) with bogus messages it must waste effort verifying; the Initiator clears only a bounded number per round (puzzles are costly). The attacker (coalition) can drive the queue to full -> expected TRUE, matching the paper's finding that the counterfeiting DoS succeeds (P ~ 0.895). Abstracts the processing-cost rewards and the puzzle-difficulty analysis.
